reason: Both conversations give the right safety stop and escalate to an electrician or engineer, and neither asks which switch trips (RCD or MCB). Both also overclaim an earth-leakage fault. Conversation 1 hedges slightly better: it raises overload as an alternative in the first turn, asks about spills and moisture, and says the engineer may find only moisture that needs drying. Conversation 2 assumes it is an RCD, then concludes the cause is 'likely internal electrical degradation' of the coil or power module, downplaying the boil-overs. That is closer to the unsupported claim of a definite hob-board fault. Conversation 2 does give better isolation advice (fused spur or consumer unit), which keeps the gap slight.
